title: An example's result.json as stored, format 2
description: What build.py writes since format 2 (examples/tools/result_format.py): each fact once. This schema checks the document's structure. Each field's own definition is in result.schema.json, which validates the flat view of the document (result_format.view()), the shape the pages are rendered from. A result recorded before has format 1: the flat result itself, with no `format` field, validated by result.schema.json alone.

claim.description: What is checked, over which scope, against which inputs (result.schema.json#/properties/claim).

attempt.description: The run as one attempt at the claim, with how it ended in `execution`, the only place format 2 keeps it (result.schema.json#/properties/attempt).

conclusion.description: What the attempt concluded: the verdict as `status`, its label, vacuity and the example's expectation, and each obligation with its own evidence.

status.description: The verdict: verified is established, violation refuted, unverifiable unresolved; null without one.

label.description: The verdict as the page shows it (the flat `verdictLabel`).

obligationKeys.description: For each kind of obligation the run stored, the flat field its obligations are shown as, in order.

evidence.description: The obligation's own record: an item of the flat `properties`, `configurations` or `modelContracts`.

Everything else the run found, under the flat names: the excerpts, existing tests, counterexamples, trace, coverage, files, and the approach's own fields. B11's headline fields (`property`, `domain`, `proof`, `problem`, `statement`) are a summary of its property obligations, kept until the format after this one computes them.

bundle.description: The evidence files the run left, with their SHA-256 (result.schema.json#/properties/bundle).
